name: Bonggo
sweep_summary: Bonggo is not in the catalog and this search of works with stress in the title's single item is a Glottolog false hit: Karsono's KIMLI 2011 paper 'Pola Unsur Suprasegmental Nada Bahasa Tionghoa Orang Surabaya' was auto-assigned to Bonggo [bpg] from the Indonesian word 'pola' (Glottolog's own language code note says 'computerized assignment from \"pola\"'); the open PDF (Petra repository, read in full, saved) is a Praat study of Mandarin Chinese lexical tone and sentence intonation as produced by non-Chinese-speaking Surabaya residents. It says nothing about Bonggo or about word stress. Glottolog's reference list for bong1287 (18 entries, saved) holds no grammar or phonology: all Bonggo-specific items are wordlists/ethnography (Grace 1956 fieldnotes, Grace 1971/1972 Sarmi-coast comparative phonology notes in Irian 1(3), Kim 2006 SIL survey report on Bgu/Kaptiau/Tarpia, 1960s Bgu kinship papers). Attempts to reach Kim 2006 on sil.org could not be reached by automated download; ScholarSpace and Wikipedia gave nothing; No first-hand statement of Bonggo word stress was found. If anyone pursues one, the Kim 2006 SIL Electronic Survey Report (47 pp., 'overview;wordlist;socling') and Grace's 1955-56 Bonggo notebook are the only candidates, both low expected yield (medium priority for Kim 2006, print/archive-only for Grace). Everything downloaded is under with.

earlier_scan.source_named: Only wordlists/surveys exist (Grace 1956 fieldnotes; Anceaux wordlists; Kim 2006 survey); no grammar or phonology of Bonggo located

sources.note: Nothing. a full-text search for stress/accent/tone gives no real hit. 'Bongo' (the region of the settlement Armopa, 139°36'E) is one of six TRIPP wordlists; 'the most complete lists were obtained for Sobei, Bongo, and Tarpia' (p. 103); content is diachronic consonant/vowel correspondences with Proto-Oceanic; Grace says the lists 'cannot make any pretense of being systematically phonemic'; no synchronic phonology, no stress marks.

sources.note: The only modern first-hand document on Bonggo/Bgu (March 2006 SIL survey; wordlists + sociolinguistics). SIL survey reports sometimes include a phonetically transcribed wordlist with stress marks or a brief phonology note; would be the first evidence of Bonggo stress placement. Apparently never issued in SIL-ESR; ask SIL Indonesia / SIL Language & Culture Archives.
